en.title: Test your knowledge: Human and Nature
en.description: Seven questions about the Human and Nature theme.
en.intro: TODO: one line about this theme for the test intro (the design repeats the Climate text "The typical weather of a place over many years.")

questions.question: What do mangroves provide?
questions.explanation: Mangrove roots protect coasts from waves and storms. They also shelter young fish and store large amounts of carbon.

questions.question: Coral reefs are…

options.text: Tiny animals that live with algae

questions.explanation: The algae give corals food and their bright colours. If the water gets too warm, corals push the algae out and turn white.

questions.question: Check all the places that shelter marine life:
questions.explanation: Mangrove roots hide young fish. Reefs cover less than 1% of the sea floor but shelter a quarter of all sea life. Open water has no structures to hide in.

questions.question: Coral reefs cover …% of the ocean floor
questions.explanation: Reefs cover less than 1% of the sea floor, yet a quarter of all sea life depends on them. They also feed fishing communities and break waves before they reach the coast.

questions.question: Forests and lakes are important to human life because they…
questions.explanation: Forests release oxygen, and forests like those around Mount Rinjani catch rain and keep drinking water clean. Lakes and rivers also supply drinking and farming water.

questions.question: The main reason coral reefs are dying is…
questions.explanation: When the sea stays too warm for too long, corals push out their algae and turn white. Bleached corals starve. At 1.5 °C of warming, 70–90% of reefs would be lost, and at 2 °C more than 99% (IPCC).

questions.question: Check all statements that are true:

options.text: Animals adapt easily to the changing circumstances
Fish don’t need oxygen in the ocean

questions.explanation: Cutting forests removes the homes of animals. Melting ice raises sea level, and dark water absorbs more heat than ice. It is thawing frozen ground that releases CO₂ and methane, so I’d reword that option.
